key_insight: Quantum-assisted training enabled a bearing-anomaly detection pipeline designed for microcontrollers, but showed no advantage over a rounded-weight classical OCSVM baseline.
engineering_relevance: The pipeline targets low-cost edge predictive maintenance with vibration features and OCSVM inference that avoids floating-point operations.
method: Extract vibration features and select them using mRMR optimized by VQE under a computing-time limit.
Train an OCSVM using a variational quantum algorithm with Pauli-correlation encoding (PCE).
Adapt OCSVM inference for microcontrollers without floating-point operations.
evidence_signal: Small-scale simulator tests on the Paderborn bearing dataset found optimal VQE selections in 36% of Adam runs; PCE beat chance before classical local search, while rounded-weight SMO matched performance without search.
watch_item: Simulator-only, small-scale results do not establish a quantum advantage or validate performance on physical quantum hardware and deployed microcontrollers.
paper_title: Predictive Maintenance at the Edge: An Embedded Anomaly Detection Pipeline Trained with Quantum Optimization
